Title: Melaka polls: Muhyiddin hopes voter support translates into votes for Bersatu
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu has described the encouraging response from voters in the seven state constituencies it is contesting in the Melaka election as a positive sign ahead of polling day on Saturday.
Its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party's campaign efforts had made good progress, judging by the encouraging turnout at its programmes in several constituencies since the campaign began.
He cited Pantai Kundor as an example, where a large crowd attended a campaign programme for Bersatu candidate Datin Seri Dr Asmah Ibrahim.
He hoped the support shown by voters throughout the campaign period would translate into votes on Nov 14.
"Based on our observations, the response from nearly half the voters in those areas (seven constituencies) has been very encouraging," he told reporters after attending the Berjalan Untuk Perubahan programme in Pantai Puteri here today.
Also present were Bersatu secretary-general and Melaka election director Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali and Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz.
Muhyiddin said candidates for the seven seats were selected based on specific qualifications, with the party also explaining its objectives and reasons for contesting in the respective constituencies.
On a related matter, Muhyiddin urged voters living outside Melaka to return home to cast their ballots on polling day.
He said higher voter participation, including among those living outside the state, was important to ensure their democratic rights were exercised.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DBKL can now issue flood warnings up to an hour in advance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) can now issue flood warnings up to one hour in advance, compared with just five minutes previously, following upgrades to the Kuala Lumpur Command Centre.
Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Lo Su Fui said the command centre's enhanced capabilities allow residents to be alerted much earlier.
He said 14 flood and flash flood hotspots had been identified in Kuala Lumpur this year, though none were located within the Batu parliamentary constituency.
"Based on records from the past five years, two locations in the Batu parliamentary constituency, Kampung Chubadak Asal and Kampung Seri Delima, have experienced flash floods, affecting a total of 250 residents," he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was replying to a question from Prabakaran M. Parameswaran (PH-Batu) on the number of residents living in flood-prone areas in Batu, the capacity of temporary evacuation centres (PPS) and the government's plans to provide medium-term temporary accommodation.
Lo said DBKL and the Social Welfare Department had coordinated 36 temporary evacuation centres with a combined capacity of 3,550 people as part of short- and medium-term measures.
On the challenges faced, he said about 70 per cent of Kuala Lumpur's original 33.5 hectares of water catchment or retention areas had been lost due to previous land alienation.
However, he said DBKL and the Federal Territories Department were working with the Selangor government to identify suitable sites for replacement retention ponds.
"In addition, the Federal Territories Department and DBKL have frozen development applications involving land on or around retention ponds and are planning to transform Kuala Lumpur into a sponge city.
"We will continue to improve DBKL's performance, particularly in tackling flooding in Kuala Lumpur," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,801 schools without computer labs to receive device rental services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is expanding its computer laboratory device rental services to 1,801 schools that lack such facilities to ensure comprehensive access to digital learning resources.
The ministry said the expansion began in the third quarter of this year as a key approach to strengthening digital facilities in schools, alongside the targeted distribution of devices to students from the low-income (B40) group.
It said the supply of computer laboratory devices was implemented in three phases from 2021 to 2023, involving the distribution of 244,158 devices to schools nationwide, regardless of location or parliamentary constituency.
To support B40 and rural students, the ministry, through Yayasan Didik Negara, also distributed 16,230 free digital education devices—comprising laptops, Chromebooks and tablets—to 257 schools nationwide between 2022 and 2026.
"This free device distribution is carried out in a targeted and transparent manner, based on needs-based criteria verified by the State Education Departments (JPN) and District Education Offices (PPD)," it said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.
The ministry was replying to a question from Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Hussein (BN-Sembrong) on the status of free digital device distribution to B40 students in rural areas and plans for high-performance internet coverage in remote school laboratories.
To improve internet access in schools, including in remote areas, the ministry provides fibre-optic facilities with speeds ranging from 300 Mbps to 800 Mbps and broadband services at 30 Mbps. Schools facing limitations in accessing terrestrial networks are provided with high-performance satellite internet services offering speeds of up to 100 Mbps.
As of October this year, 8,955 schools (87.28 per cent) out of 10,259 MOE educational institutions nationwide had internet access through fibre-optic technology, the ministry said.
The remaining institutions, which still rely on wireless broadband and satellite technology, are being upgraded in phases based on technical feasibility at their respective locations.

Title: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of US curbs
Article:
BEIJING: Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China, worried that the scandal involving the US chipmaker's CEO Jensen Huang could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their remote use of advanced processors, three people familiar with the matter said.
Seeking to protect US dominance of the critical sector, Washington restricts exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips. But Chinese companies can access such processors remotely by renting computing power at data centres overseas.
The current move to secure rented capacity points to growing concern among Chinese technology companies that the gap in US export controls may now be closed.
A major Chinese cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have contacted data-centre operators about reserving it, the people said. The people declined to be identified, or to identify the cloud provider, due to the sensitivity of the matter.
Smaller AI labs are considering similar steps, including approaching major providers of rented computing power in Southeast Asia, two of the people said.
The companies fear the controversy surrounding Huang could add political momentum to the Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, a US bill that would give the Commerce Department authority to regulate remote, cloud-based access to restricted technology, the people said. The House of Representatives passed the bill in January by a 369-22 vote, and it awaits Senate action.
Advanced Nvidia processors are used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products. Restricting overseas cloud access would make it harder for Chinese developers to obtain high-end computing power without importing the chips directly.
CHINESE SPY ALLEGATIONS TRIGGER US SCRUTINY
Nvidia's Huang said on Sunday that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The New York Times reported that the woman involved was Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed, and that US authorities had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset. Jensen and Alice Huang are not related.
Reuters could not independently verify that allegation, which China has denied.
Megaspeed has faced scrutiny from US authorities over suspicions it helped Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips that were subject to US export controls. The company has denied illegally diverting chips to China.
In a statement on Thursday, Megaspeed said it had cooperated with inspections by the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security and hired a leading US law firm to conduct a comprehensive inventory of its graphics processing units and independently verify its export-control compliance practices.
It said it welcomed government scrutiny and was committed to complying with US export-control laws.
Nvidia and the US Commerce Department did not respond to requests for comment.
Shares of Chinese AI companies fell sharply in Hong Kong on Thursday amid concerns that the controversy could lead to tighter US restrictions on access to advanced chips. Alibaba fell as much as 7.1 per cent while AI model developers Z.AI and MiniMax both dropped at least 7.0 per cent.
Alice Huang had business dealings and investment ties with several leading Chinese technology companies, including Tencent and Alibaba, according to two people familiar with the matter.
Tencent said its computing procurement, leasing and operations complied with applicable laws and regulations, including export controls.
"We have no knowledge of, nor involvement in, any alleged unlawful activities referenced in these reports, nor do we have any business dealings or investment ties with the individuals concerned," the company said.
Alibaba did not respond to a request for comment.
GREY-MARKET BUYING SURGES AMID FEARS OF SMUGGLING CRACKDOWN
The prospect of tougher enforcement has also fuelled demand for restricted Nvidia AI chips in China's grey market, prompting traders and intermediaries to start stockpiling these processors, two of the people said.
They said buyers fear the controversy could prompt a broader US crackdown on smuggling of advanced chips and AI servers into China.
A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, highlighting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology.
US prosecutors in March charged Super Micro Computer co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and two others with conspiring to divert servers containing Nvidia chips to China through a Southeast Asia-based company.
Prosecutors said the company bought about US$2.5 billion of servers from Super Micro between 2024 and 2025, and that a substantial portion was diverted to China. The defendants have not been convicted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police chase ends with four men arrested after car crashes into drain
Article:
PENDANG: Four men were arrested after their car skidded into a drain while fleeing police in Jalan Kampung Bendang Raja, Kubur Panjang, here yesterday.
In the 6.30pm incident, the Proton Persona carrying the four suspects, aged between 33 and 51, failed to stop when ordered by police.
District police chief Superintendent Rodzi Abu Hassan said the driver sped off and swerved into a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) from the Pendang police headquarters' Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department, causing the two vehicles to graze each other before the car skidded into a drain on the left side of the road.
He said checks found all four local men injured, and they were taken to Pendang Hospital for treatment.
"Further checks on the suspects and their vehicle uncovered six transparent plastic packets of various sizes suspected to contain syabu and one transparent plastic packet suspected to contain heroin," he said in a statement today.
Rodzi said background checks showed the 48-year-old suspect had a criminal record with 15 prior offences, while the 51-year-old had five.
The other two suspects, aged 34 and 33, had two prior criminal offences each, he added.
"Initial urine screening tests found all of them positive for amphetamine, methamphetamine and morphine.
"Three suspects have been remanded for four days from today until Nov 15 under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to assist in the investigation, while the remaining suspect was released on police bail due to health reasons," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, Section 186 of the Penal Code, and Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM208.3mil allocated to upgrade Mada irrigation and drainage systems in 2027
Article:
Bernama
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has allocated RM208.319 million next year to strengthen irrigation and drainage systems in Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) areas, including upgrading works, developing new water sources and rehabilitating the Pedu Dam in Kedah.
Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the initiative aims to ensure more efficient water resource management, particularly in tackling unpredictable rainfall patterns and lower reservoir levels compared with previous years.
He said Mada is also enhancing water resource monitoring through a telemetry system to continuously track reservoir levels, rainfall distribution and resource changes to guide management planning.
"In addition, the efficiency of the irrigation system is being improved through the operation of 117 water reuse pumps, maximising rainwater utilisation, water-flow control, as well as the maintenance of water control structures to ensure more efficient water distribution," he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was replying to a question from Datuk Awang Hashim (PN-Pendang) on the government's plans to strengthen irrigation and drainage systems in Mada areas to address unpredictable rainfall and low dam water levels.
Chan said the government is also adjusting padi planting schedules and practices based on water availability, promoting drought-resistant padi varieties and implementing six rounds of Cloud Seeding Operations (OPA) throughout 2026.
These measures are supported by the development and maintenance of 15 Tertiary Blocks and the Jeniang Water Transfer Scheme, which is expected to be completed by 2030 through a public-private partnership.
Replying to a supplementary question from Awang on the progress of tertiary irrigation projects and flood complaints in the Tokai area, Chan said Phase One of the project, involving 12 blocks, had recorded 25.81 per cent physical progress as of Oct 26, exceeding its 25.19 per cent target.
This puts the project 0.62 percentage points ahead of schedule, with full completion expected by 2030, he said.
On allegations that inadequate drainage had caused water to enter homes in the area, he said the ministry will instruct Mada officers to visit the affected locations to monitor the situation and gather direct feedback from residents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MYDCD's net profits nears RM26mil in Q1 FY27 ahead of ACE Market listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ahead of its debut on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on Nov 17, MyDCD Bhd reported a net profit of RM25.71 million on revenue of RM178.68 million for its first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), supported by strong contributions from its data centre infrastructure business.
The investment holding company, which operates through its subsidiary DCD Technology Sdn Bhd, recorded a profit before tax of RM34.06 million and gross profit of RM37.79 million for its first interim quarterly financial report.
As at Sept 30, 2026, MyDCD had an outstanding order book of approximately RM1.32 billion, providing earnings visibility as it continues to execute its secured projects.
Of the total, RM1.27 billion came from the integration of mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection (MEPF) systems for data centres, which is expected to be recognised progressively until the financial year ending June 30, 2028.
The remaining RM53.08 million comprised maintenance services and parts, with revenue recognition expected to extend until FY32.
The group said its data centre MEPF integration business accounted for approximately 96.85 per cent of total revenue during the quarter, reflecting its focus on critical infrastructure.
Chief executive officer Chris Ow Yong said continued investments in data centres, driven by growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing, were expected to sustain demand for specialised MEPF installation works.
He noted that Malaysia's information and communications industry recorded a 68.2 per cent increase in approved private investments to RM103.3 billion in the first half of 2026, reflecting continued investor interest in digital infrastructure.
Looking ahead, Ow Yong said the group planned to strengthen its operational capabilities through additional recruitment, staff training and office expansion.
It also intends to invest in a centralised enterprise resource planning system and information technology infrastructure to improve operational efficiency.
The group remains optimistic about its prospects, supported by continued data centre investments, its existing order book and planned expansion initiatives.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Residents recount terror as foreign man goes on rampage at Aman Dua apartment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Residents of Aman Dua Apartment were left terrified after a foreign man went on a rampage, chasing people and forcing neighbours to lock themselves inside their homes.
Muhammad Aidil Roslan, 26, said he witnessed the incident from his third-floor apartment, which faces the suspect's unit.
The furniture maker, who has lived at the apartment for a year, said the suspect had been behaving unusually in the two weeks leading up to the incident.
"For the past two weeks, he had frequently argued with his housemate. We could hear him shouting and making a lot of noise," he said when met at the apartment.
Aidil said the situation became particularly frightening when the man began chasing anyone who crossed his path.
"When he came towards my house, I immediately went inside and locked the door because I was afraid he would come after me."
He also saw a woman leaving the suspect's unit bleeding, after which the man appeared to be alone.
Aidil said the incident was particularly shocking as the apartment complex had generally been peaceful.
"Seeing what happened to the policemen was frightening and heartbreaking. They were just carrying out their duties, and suddenly something like this happened," he said.
A policeman's hand was
severed
during the attack.
Another resident, Tan, 58, who has lived at the apartment for more than 25 years, described the suspect as someone who had previously been pleasant and regularly greeted his neighbours.
"He was usually a pleasant man. Whenever we crossed paths, he would greet me. It was only a month ago that his behaviour started changing," he said.
Tan said the suspect's friends had visited the apartment because they were concerned about his behaviour and had contacted the police for help.
He said the man later attacked a police officer with a parang before returning to his unit to change his clothes.
"He then made his way downstairs and began targeting any policeman he saw. He also damaged a police car with the parang he was holding," he said.
Tan said the suspect eventually left the apartment compound and went to a nearby mini-mart before he was shot dead.
Despite the incident, Tan cautioned against blaming the wider foreign community living at the apartment.
He said African nationals made up about five per cent of the residents and had generally lived peacefully alongside locals.
"This was an isolated incident. We should not label all foreigners as bad because of what one person did.
"They are usually unproblematic. I have lived here for more than 25 years, and something like this should not change how we view the entire community," he said.
Aidil also described the incident as the first of its kind he had witnessed at the apartment.
However, he hoped the authorities would strengthen checks on foreigners who misused immigration documents or remained in the country unlawfully.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Second landslide reported in Sungai Besi, a day after Shah Alam incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A landslide has occurred
behind PPR Seri Malaysia near Kampung Malaysia
in Sungai Besi, with large chunks of concrete collapsing onto a pathway.
Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud confirmed the incident, saying personnel from the police, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Fire and Rescue Department had been dispatched to assess the situation.
No casualties were reported, he told the New Straits Times.
Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar said firefighters from the Sungai Besi Fire and Rescue Station had also been deployed to monitor the situation.
The incident comes a day after a landslide at Persiaran Kosmos, Section U5, Shah Alam, damaged a retaining wall and affected a residential area.
In that incident, sections of a concrete retaining wall collapsed, exposing the soil beneath a building at the top of the slope.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pharmaniaga's net profits surges on RM16mil tax benefits
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pharmaniaga Bhd's net profit for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) surged 261 per cent to RM26.3 million from RM7.3 million a year earlier, as it recorded RM16.4 million tax benefits.
Profit before zakat and taxation (PBT) rose to RM13 million from RM10.4 million previously, supported by interest savings of RM3.2 million following the partial repayment of borrowings and continued operational efficiency efforts.
The group declared a dividend of 0.32 sen per share for the quarter.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026 (9M FY26), Pharmaniaga's net profit increased 72.1 per cent to RM70.2 million from RM40.8 million in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue grew 8.2 per cent to RM3.23 billion from RM2.99 billion, primarily driven by stronger demand in its concession segment.
PBT increased 22 per cent to RM77.2 million from RM63.3 million, with the group recording interest savings of RM17.4 million following the partial repayment of borrowings using proceeds from its regularisation plan.
Looking ahead, Pharmaniaga said the government's 2027 budget for healthcare of RM47.7 billion would provide a supportive backdrop for the industry.
The group is also expanding its biopharmaceutical portfolio after securing National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency approval for EVnyx, an Enterovirus 71 vaccine, and ISENDA (liraglutide), its first generic glucagon-like peptide-1 product targeting Type 2 diabetes and weight management.
It plans to launch nine new pharmaceutical products in 2027, focusing on cardiovascular, oncology, anti-infectives and vaccines.
Meanwhile, the group expects the number of products under its Approved Product Purchase List concession to increase from about 850 to more than 1,200 within the concession period.
Pharmaniaga is also progressing with the equipping of four strategically located warehouses, with full operations targeted to commence in the first quarter of 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH needs support from all communities to bring change, says Anwar
Article:
MELAKA: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants people of all races in Melaka to unite and support the 24 Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates contesting in the state election, with polling scheduled for this Saturday.
The PH chairman said support from all communities was needed to bring about change in Melaka by giving PH the responsibility of administering the state.
"I am here to show my support for (PH candidate for Machap Jaya) Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin.
"We want to bring about change.
"I urge all Chinese, Indians, Malays, Orang Asli and everyone else to unite in supporting PH," the prime minister said during a walkabout at the Kampung Baru Machap night market.
Also present were PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Wanita PKR chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek and Lim.
Earlier, Anwar spent about half an hour mingling with people, including traders, during a walkabout with PH candidate for Paya Rumput Datuk Zainal Abidin.
He arrived at Taman Krubong Jaya about 6.05pm, where hundreds of people and traders had gathered to await his arrival. He took time to shake hands and speak with voters before leaving.
He was scheduled to attend Ngopi Santai sessions in Ayer Molek, followed by the Jelajah Harapan Melaka Rumah Kita programme in Hang Tuah Jaya and the Pesta Melaka Rumah Kita in Alor Gajah.
PH is fielding 24 candidates in the Melaka election, including in the five seats it currently holds: Bukit Katil, Ayer Keroh, Kesidang, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Palace crisis in Negri Sembilan to be resolved soon, says MB
Article:
TAMPIN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is confident that the crisis involving the state royal institution will be resolved soon.
He said the matter had been discussed at both state and national Umno leadership levels, with talks pointing towards a positive outcome.
"The ongoing crisis will indeed be resolved soon.
"Discussions have also been held with top Umno leaders. Through these discussions, we are moving towards a positive resolution of all issues in Negri Sembilan," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating the state-level World Town Planning Day 2026 celebration at Kompleks Arena here today.
Yesterday, Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi expressed confidence that the crisis in Negri Sembilan would be
resolved soon
.
The Umno president said he hoped a solution could be reached through a spirit of togetherness among the parties involved, as had previously enabled the formation of the state government.
"I am confident that whatever problems we are facing in Negri Sembilan have reached their final stages. We pray that the issues will be resolved soon," he said.
On plans to hold a five-day state assembly sitting from Nov 26, Ismail said the state government was still awaiting the consent of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
"We are still waiting for Tuanku's consent," said the Juasseh assemblyman.
However, Ismail declined to comment on claims that he had changed his position and renewed his support for Tuanku Muhriz, despite having signed a proclamation calling for the ruler's removal on Aug 3.
Asked about criticism from a coalition of 15 Negeri Sembilan non-governmental organisations (NGOs) over his handling of the crisis, he said he had yet to read their statement.
"I have not seen it yet as I was busy in Sendayan this morning attending the opening of a Rolls-Royce factory.
"Whatever it is, I am working to do my best for the people of Negri Sembilan. Everything is moving in a positive direction," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Injured policeman warned public to flee despite being in pain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Despite being seriously injured after an attack by a parang-wielding man, a policeman still managed to warn members of the public to leave the scene in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, last night.
The moment was shared by a Threads user, skchau1985, who said the video was recorded at the scene.
The user said the officer, while in pain, urged those nearby to leave as the area was dangerous.
"I'm in pain. It's dangerous here, leave quickly," the user quoted the officer as saying.
The user also expressed sadness and admiration for the officer's concern for others despite his injuries.
"The news spread everywhere throughout the night. This is the footage I recorded.
"I was touched and heartbroken. I hope you recover," the user wrote.
The post included a video showing the officer receiving initial treatment from ambulance personnel at the scene.
In the incident at 7pm yesterday, Lance Corporal Thierry Rodger Pendy, 26, suffered serious injuries, including the severing of his right hand, after being attacked by a man armed with two parangs at an apartment in Desa Aman Puri.
The Gombak police headquarters personnel was initially taken to Selayang Hospital before being transferred to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) for surgery.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad today confirmed that the eight-hour operation to reattach the officer's hand was successful.
The suspect, believed to be a foreigner, was shot dead by police while they were attempting to arrest him near a playground not far from the scene.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Subsidised cooking oil tracking system still has gaps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's system for tracking subsidised cooking oil cannot identify buyers, leaving gaps that allow leakages and misuse, Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said.
He said the electronic Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme (eCOSS), introduced in May 2023, could track supplies delivered to retailers but not identify buyers.
"We know how much is supplied and the quota reaching retailers, but we do not have data on who buys the cooking oil," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Armizan was winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for his ministry.
He said some retailers had allegedly stored subsidised cooking oil packets before selling them in bulk to certain parties.
Others had reportedly opened the packets and transferred the contents into bottles for resale at higher prices.
To address the gaps, Armizan said the ministry had introduced the Mobile eCOSS application, which requires consumers to scan a QR code when buying subsidised cooking oil packets.
He said the system would help authorities identify buyers, monitor purchases and improve subsidy targeting.
Although the requirement had drawn complaints from consumers, Armizan said the data was necessary to curb leakages.
"Leakages are still occurring. I do not deny that, but compared with before, there has been a reduction," he said.
Armizan said enforcement had also been strengthened, while the ministry had revised the distribution system to improve access to subsidised cooking oil.
Under the new arrangement, repackaging companies determine 50 per cent of distribution destinations, while the ministry's state and district offices decide where the remaining supplies should be delivered.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor Plantations posts RM100mil net profit in Q3 2026, declares 1.50 sen dividend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Plantations Group Bhd (JPG) reported a net profit of RM100.32 million for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), representing a 5.45 per cent decline from RM106.04 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Despite the year-on-year moderation, the group demonstrated a robust sequential recovery, with net profit surging 96 per cent quarter-on-quarter from the RM51.2 million posted in the immediate preceding quarter.
According to the group's financial statements, revenue for Q3 FY26 stood at RM450.72 million, a 9.2 per cent contraction from RM496.15 million a year ago. However, against the preceding quarter, revenue grew by 8.4 per cent from RM415.84 million.
The revenue decline was largely attributed to lower delivery volumes, with crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel (PK) deliveries falling by 15.9 per cent and 10.4 per cent, respectively.
This drop in volume was partially offset by stronger selling prices, with the average CPO selling price 6.5 per cent higher in Q3 FY26 at RM4,683 per tonne, compared with in Q3 FY25. Similarly, the average PK selling price rose by 6.6 per cent to RM3,747 per tonne.
The group faced rising operational expenses during the quarter, with internal CPO cost of production increasing by 13.5 per cent from a year ago, to RM2,526 per tonne.
However, the impressive quarterly profit rebound was heavily driven by a 35.6 per cent surge in fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production, which reached 292,352 tonnes in line with the seasonal peak crop cycle.
This higher output allowed fixed costs to be spread over a larger volume, effectively lowering the internal CPO cost of production by 9.4 per cent sequentially from RM2,788 per tonne.
For the cumulative nine-month period, JPG's net profit contracted by 21.3 per cent to RM201.93 million, driven by higher production and operating costs, alongside lower finance income. Its revenue slipped 0.9 per cent during the period to RM1.22 billion.
The board of directors approved and declared a third interim single-tier dividend of 1.50 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026. The dividend, totaling approximately RM37.38 million, will be payable on Dec 10.
Looking ahead to the final quarter of 2026, JPG anticipates CPO prices to remain broadly range-bound.
The group noted that while biodiesel demand and seasonal consumption will provide support, elevated inventory levels may constrain significant price upside.
"Prolonged dry conditions and the potential lagged effects of El Niño on yields remain key uncertainties affecting the production outlook," said JPG.
Indonesia's B50 biodiesel programme remains a structural demand driver, though its impact will depend on domestic production and consumption trends.
The group also acknowledged impending cost pressures from the higher minimum wage, which is expected to increase labour costs across the plantation sector.
In response, JPG remains focused on improving productivity, accelerating mechanisation, and maintaining strict cost discipline to mitigate these pressures while advancing its strategic growth initiatives.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Stronger BN-PN cooperation in Melaka offers hope for GE16
Article:
MELAKA: Umno is confident that its political cooperation with Pas and Perikatan Nasional can be strengthened and extended to the federal level ahead of the 16th General Election.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the cooperation forged for the Melaka election had made more comprehensive progress compared with the understanding reached during the Negri Sembilan polls.
He said both coalitions were now coordinating their campaign efforts by bringing their operations rooms together and mobilising their respective party machinery jointly.
"This time, in the Melaka election, we have not only achieved cooperation and understanding in seats where we are not contesting against each other, but our party machinery is also working in an integrated manner.
"There are no separate operations rooms. Everything has been brought together, and even the Wanita, Youth and Puteri wings are being mobilised jointly.
"The liveliest ceramah are also those organised by Barisan Nasional and PN," he told reporters when met at an event with Indian Muslim voters in Pengkalan Batu earlier.
Also present were BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Malaysian Indian Muslim Congress (Kimma) president Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Kader.
BN candidate for Ayer Molek Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali, BN candidate for Pengkalan Batu Siti Aisyah Mahmood and PN candidate for Ayer Keroh Michael Gan were also present.
On the possibility of extending the cooperation to the national level, Asyraf Wajdi said he believed the current understanding had given both sides the confidence to formalise closer ties.
"With this level of understanding, we (Umno) are very confident that we can forge closer cooperation between BN and PN to face the General Election.
"In fact, this cooperation will not only extend to parliamentary seats, but also to states currently administered by PN (namely Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu)," he added.
In the Melaka election, BN is contesting 23 state seats, while PN is contesting five of the 28 seats. The Election Commission has set this Saturday as polling day.

Title: Najib's return home brings relief to family, says daughter
Article:
MELAKA: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's return home to serve his house arrest has brought relief and joy to his family after four years apart, his daughter Nooryana Najwa Najib said.
She said her father looked visibly relieved when he stepped through the door and was happy to be reunited with his wife and other family members after their long separation.
"I managed to meet him on Tuesday night. After that, I travelled to Melaka, but we are very grateful that the family could see him.
"He felt relieved upon arriving home because he had faced various emotional and mental pressures during the four years away from his family," she said when met at the Tangga Batu parliamentary command centre here.
On Sept 18, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
Nooryana said her family would comply with and respect all conditions set by the prison authorities regarding her father's house arrest.
"My family and I are very grateful that Datuk Seri Najib has returned home and begun his house arrest. I would like to express our thanks and appreciation to the prison authorities who took good care of him," she said.
On the Melaka state election, Nooryana said Barisan Nasional (BN) had an advantage in fielding young candidates because it was putting forward individuals with experience and the trust of voters to serve as future party leaders.
She said BN welcomed the participation of young candidates from various parties as a positive development for democracy. However, the coalition prioritised candidates who had already earned voters' confidence over newcomers who still had to build recognition and support.
"They do not just come and contest to represent a generation of young leaders, but they are leaders who have experience, have served and have a track record.
"We welcome all young candidates, and I think everyone should be given a chance. However, on BN's part, we always prioritise candidates whom we feel have already gained the confidence and trust of the residents," she said.
On the expected turnout among young voters, she said the "fear of missing out" phenomenon and the use of social media in political campaigning were unavoidable trends.
She said young people's enthusiasm for participating in the democratic process was positive, adding that BN's responsibility was to explain its offerings, which she described as better for young people than those of rival parties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Zahid lauds Kimma's decades of loyalty to Umno, BN
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has praised the Malaysian Indian Muslim Congress (Kimma) for its unwavering loyalty, crediting the party for consistently supporting Umno and BN over several decades of elections.
The Umno president said Kimma had stood by the party for more than 30 years as a trusted ally, making it an important part of BN's support base.
Founded in 1976 to champion the socioeconomic and political interests of Malaysia's Indian Muslim community, Kimma has long sought full component party membership in BN.
Although it remains outside BN's formal Supreme Council structure, it was granted associate member status with Umno in 2010.
"In every by-election and state election campaign, Kimma has shown its own resolve and worked tirelessly to gather Indian Muslim voters to support BN candidates," Zahid said at a gathering hosted by Kimma in Pengkalan Batu.
"I see that Indian Muslim voters in Melaka remain deeply loyal and steadfast with BN," he added, while thanking KIMMA president Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Kader for his leadership in mobilising support.
Zahid also called on the community to extend its support to Perikatan Nasional candidates, including PN candidate for Ayer Keroh Michael Gan, under the electoral pact between the two coalitions, with BN contesting 23 seats and PN five.
Kimma president Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Kader said the party had activated its grassroots machinery across all 28 constituencies in Melaka, including setting up a dedicated call centre, to ensure the state's estimated 2,850 Indian Muslim voters turned out on polling day.
"Through our Jalinan Rakyat  network, we have already compiled voter data and met with them even before candidate nominations," he said.
"On Nov 14, our call centre will contact voters to remind them to cast their ballots and assist those who need transport or face any issues. Our task is to ensure every Indian Muslim voter is brought out to vote."
Syed Ibrahim added that supporting BN was a strict party directive, warning that members who failed to support the coalition risked being expelled.
Indian Muslims account for about three per cent of Melaka's electorate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar chairs special meeting to step up Selangor flood response
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim chaired a special meeting at Parliament House today to streamline coordination in tackling recurring floods in Selangor.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting focused on four key actions, beginning with strengthening early warning systems with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and improving disaster management coordination through the Selangor State Disaster Management Committee.
The other two measures involve resolving flash floods through the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) and studying Kuala Lumpur City Hall's (DBKL) flood management best practices.
"Special attention is being given to flood-prone areas, particularly in the Petaling and Kuala Selangor districts, which recorded 1,180 evacuees at seven temporary relief centres as of Nov 12, 2026.
"I want every one of these actions implemented immediately, including accelerating flood mitigation efforts and upgrading drainage systems to reduce the risk of recurring floods," he said in a social media post.
Amirudin said the meeting was also attended by state government representatives, state executive councillors, state assemblymen, district officers and relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), DID, the Public Works Department (PWD) and the Selangor Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU).
He added that the welfare of flood victims remains a priority, including channelling the RM3,000 Selangor People's Flood Disaster Special Aid to each eligible head of household, subject to set conditions.
"I understand the people's anxiety, especially those who repeatedly face floods. Therefore, I want every plan translated into immediate, tangible action, not just discussions," he said.

Title: Khaled confident BN-PN cooperation will deliver Melaka victory
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Strong cooperation between the Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional machinery can help the coalition secure victory in the 16th Melaka election
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said he was confident that voters in the state wanted an outcome favouring BN and PN.
While all contesting parties were confident of winning, the actual outcome would only be known after voting was completed, he added.
"If you ask me, as someone from BN-PN, I would say BN-PN will win. If you ask the other side, they would also say they will win. So, let us wait for polling day.
"But we are confident that the people want the outcome to favour BN and PN," he said when asked to comment on the prospects of BN-PN cooperation in the 16th Melaka election.

Title: Keyfield's EPS fell to 14.9 sen in 9M FY26
Article:
Dhaanieyaa Lekham
KUALA LUMPUR: Keyfield Group Bhd's earnings per share declined to 14.9 sen as of end September 2026, compared with 15.93 sen in the corresponding period, as its net profits declined 6.0 per cent year on year to RM120.6 million.
At the same time, the number of ordinary shares of Keyfield increased to 809.5 million units during the period ended Sept 30, 2026 (9M FY26), from 805.9 million a year ago.
The lower net profits for the 9M FY26 was in line with a 5.1 per cent decline in revenue during the period, to RM333.2 million, from RM351.1 million in the corresponding period last year.
In the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, Keyfield's net profits stayed at RM41.4 million, just a tad higher than the RM41.34 million recorded a year ago, despite registering 30.4 per cent higher revenue of RM172.5 million.
Nevertheless, Keyfield's group chief executive officer and executive director Datuk Darren Kee Chit Huei said the business' prospects were improving following a challenging first half of 2026.
He said demand for its vessels remained robust in Malaysia and international markets, particularly the Middle East and Thailand, with utilisation rates expected to improve in the coming quarters.
Utilisation of its own vessels increased to 89 per cent in Q3 FY26 from 81.4 per cent a year earlier, reflecting stronger chartering activities and efforts to meet customer requirements.
International operations contributed 18.2 per cent of quarterly revenue, compared with 6.8 per cent in Q3 FY25.
Kee said the stronger revenue growth did not translate into a similar increase in earnings due to moderated charter rates for its own accommodation workboats and a higher contribution from third-party vessels, which carry lower gross profit margins.
The group expects stronger offshore activity in 2027 and 2028 to provide further growth opportunities.
In October 2026, Keyfield took delivery of Inai Kenanga, which will be renamed Keyfield Karuna, a mega trailing suction hopper dredger, marking its entry into the dredging industry.
The vessel is undergoing refurbishment and reactivation works, with commercial operations expected to begin in 2027.
Together with its cable-laying barge, Keyfield Blessing, the acquisition forms part of the group's strategy to expand beyond oil and gas offshore vessel services into a broader marine solutions provider.
The group declared an interim dividend of two sen per share, unchanged from the corresponding quarter a year ago.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Marine police seize RM670,571 in untaxed liquor and cigarettes in Kulai
Article:
KULAI: A 34-year-old man was arrested after marine police seized untaxed liquor and cigarettes worth RM670,571.94 in a warehouse raid.
Marine Police Region Two commander Assistant Commissioner Noor Azman Jamal said the operation was conducted at 5pm yesterday at a storage premises next to a workers' hostel.
The man's passport was also seized.
Noor Azman said the operation was carried out by an intelligence team from the Tampoi marine police unit following public tip-offs about smuggling activities.
Police seized 12,074 cans of beer, 526 bottles of wine and 896 cartons of untaxed cigarettes.
The liquor was valued at RM451,947.94, while the cigarettes were worth RM218,624.
The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.

Title: Melaka PH vows to scrap 7 appointed assembly seats
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan (PH) has pledged to repeal the state law allowing the appointment of seven Melaka assemblymen if it wins the 16th state election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the savings from abolishing the appointed seats would be channelled towards homeownership assistance for young people and programmes to develop young entrepreneurs.
He said the proposal was part of PH's Aspirasi Melaka Rumah Kita manifesto, which focuses on residents' needs, particularly those of the younger generation.
"The provision allowing seven appointed assembly members was approved by the State Legislative Assembly under the previous Barisan Nasional administration.
"If the people of Melaka give PH the mandate, we will abolish these seven appointed seats," he told a daily press conference at the PH operations centre in Bukit Baru today.
Adly said PH also planned to reopen the chief minister's official residence at Seri Bendahara for regular meet-the-people sessions if it returned to power.
He said the initiative, introduced during PH's administration in 2018, would allow residents to raise concerns directly with state leaders and seek solutions.
"We held these sessions every Friday when PH governed Melaka, and many of the issues raised could be resolved through direct engagement between residents and state leaders," he said.
Adly, who is also PH's Bukit Katil candidate, called on voters to support the coalition's candidates, who are contesting 24 of the state's 28 seats.
He said PH wanted the opportunity to demonstrate its ability to represent constituents, address local concerns and deliver on its election pledges.
"Give us the opportunity to serve in the Melaka State Assembly. We want to prove our capabilities through constituency work, legislative action and policies that deliver on our pledges. Your vote is a trust we will not squander," he said.
Adly also called on Melaka voters living outside the state to plan their journeys home ahead of polling this Saturday.
He encouraged voters to cast their ballots early, preferably in the morning, as rain was common in the afternoon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New 11.7km Central Spine Road stretch opens, easing Pahang-Kelantan travel
Article:
LIPIS: Motorists travelling between Pahang and Kelantan, as well as residents here, now enjoy faster and more comfortable connectivity following the official opening of a new 11.7km stretch of the Central Spine Road (LTU) project today.
The opening ceremony was jointly officiated by Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi.
Nanta said the 11.7km stretch comprises three main routes, led by the 6.95 km LTU Section 3J from Kampung Seberang Jelai to Kampung Relong, built at a cost of RM339.7 million to JKR R5 four-lane, dual-carriageway standards.
Also opened are the 3.55km Kechau Link Road, running from the Kechau Interchange to Section 3J, and the 1.2 km Link Road 4A, connecting Interchange 4A to the exit ramp.
"The project also involved the construction of five bridges, two vehicular box culverts (VBCs), the installation of street lighting and utility relocation works to ensure user safety and comfort.
"The main Kelantan-Pahang network, LTU, is a 299.4 km toll-free highway connecting Kuala Krai in Kelantan to the East Coast Expressway (LPT) Interchange in Pahang at a total cost of about RM7.7 billion," he said.
He said the Pahang alignment spans 169.1 km and is divided into 15 sections.
"Of this total, 13 sections spanning 136.8 km have been completed in phases since 2013 and opened to the public.
"The remaining two, namely Section 4B (Ladang Jerkoh to Sega Lama) and Section (Sertik to the LPT Interchange), are still under construction," he said.
Nanta said the completion of Section 3J follows the opening of Section 5A (Raub Bypass) in 2024 and will serve as a key alternative to Federal Route FT08, easing congestion, cutting travel time and fuel costs, and spurring local economic activity.
Touching on contractor commitment and maintenance, he described the project's completion as a meaningful achievement for the main contractor in overcoming various challenges, including a sharp rise in building material prices caused by global economic uncertainty following conflict in the Middle East.
He said these challenges did not deter the contractor from delivering the project on schedule without compromising quality and safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aumas secures vital pond access in Bukit Mantri dispute as court sets aside earlier injunction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mining operator Aumas Resources Bhd has secured a key interim court order ensuring its wholly-owned subsidiary, Wullersdorf Resources Sdn Bhd (WRSB), retains access to a critical water treatment pond at its Bukit Mantri tailings storage facility.
The High Court of Sabah and Sarawak at Tawau delivered its decisions on Nov 3 regarding two pivotal applications in the ongoing consolidated legal suits between Aumas and WRSB against Southsea Gold Sdn Bhd (SGSB) and Datuk Lo Fui Ming.
Broad grounds of the decision were received by WRSB's legal counsel on Wednesday, Nov 11.
The court's ruling on the inter partes application favored operational continuity and environmental safety, noting a departmental letter regarding acidic seepage flowing toward the pond.
In this case, the court recognized a "present need to keep the water containment system functioning" and found a serious issue to be tried regarding WRSB's right to use the pond and adjoining land.
Under the new order, Lo and SGSB are strictly prohibited from demolishing, physically blocking, or filling in the pond. They are also barred from preventing WRSB personnel and contractors from utilizing existing access routes to inspect, pump, treat, or neutralize the water.
However, the WRSB is not authorized to expand the pond, build new pipes, or conduct work contrary to regulatory directives. The mining company must also provide SGSB with 24 hours' written notice before executing physical repairs, barring immediate safety emergencies.
In a concurrent decision, the court allowed an application by Lo and SGSB to set aside a previous ex-parte injunction (the third injunction) originally obtained by Aumas on August 14.
Although the 21-day injunction had already expired on Sept 4, the court reviewed the matter and held it should not have been granted in its recorded terms.
The court noted, however, that there was no finding that Aumas or WRSB deliberately misled the court.
Aumas and WRSB were ordered to pay costs to the defendants. Any potential inquiry into damages caused by the injunction will require a separate application supported by proper evidence, the court ordered.
Aumas board of directors expects no material financial or operational impact on the group from these rulings.
The court clarified that these interim decisions do not determine the ultimate ownership of the disputed land, nor do they settle claims of trespass, environmental offenses, or the validity of mining scheme approvals.
Regulatory authorities will continue their lawful inspections, the court added.
The next trial dates for the consolidated suits are scheduled between Feb 23 and Feb 26, 2027.

Title: Police to investigate man seen dangling cat outside truck
Article:
KLUANG: A man was caught on video
holding a string attached to a cat

Title: Govt targets further cut in cooking oil subsidy quota
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government plans to further reduce the subsidised cooking oil quota to 50,000 metric tonnes, using the savings to help stabilise bottled cooking oil prices.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the quota had already been reduced from 66,000 to 55,000 metric tonnes.
He said the reduction was part of efforts to improve subsidy management and curb leakages under the Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme.
"We have managed to reduce the quota to 55,000 metric tonnes, and we are targeting a further reduction to 50,000," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Armizan was winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for his ministry.
He said the Cabinet had previously directed the ministry to gradually reduce the quota to 45,000 metric tonnes, but the target had not been achieved for nearly a decade.
He said savings from the programme would be used to support measures aimed at keeping bottled cooking oil affordable.
Armizan said the Cabinet had approved the proposal last Friday amid rising crude palm oil prices.
He said crude palm oil prices reached RM4,400 per tonne in October, potentially pushing the price of a 5kg bottle of cooking oil to RM34.
However, government intervention had enabled the ceiling price to remain at RM30.90.
Armizan said the cooking oil subsidy programme had placed a substantial financial burden on the government.
Although RM1 billion had been allocated for the programme under Budget 2027, actual expenditure had reached between RM1.7 billion and RM1.9 billion in some previous years, he said.
He said the government would continue reviewing the subsidy mechanism to ensure savings could be achieved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eco World, NS Corp to explore water desalination plant in Negeri Sembilan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eco World Development Group Bhd (EcoWorld) is exploring the development of a water desalination treatment plant in Negeri Sembilan for industrial water supply solutions for industrial parks developed under the Eco World brand there.
The property developer has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with NS Corporation to jointly undertake feasibility studies on developing an alternative and supplementary source of industrial water in the state.
EcoWorld said the collaboration reflects an opportunity for public-private sector cooperation to accelerate water infrastructure development in the state and enhance the competitiveness of its industrial developments.
The MoU also covers other industrial parks that EcoWorld may develop in Negeri Sembilan in the future.
The move comes amid growing investment momentum in the state, which recorded RM41.5 billion in approved investments from 2023 to June 2026.
Domestic direct investments accounted for RM24.2 billion, or 58 per cent, while foreign direct investments contributed RM17.3 billion, or 42 per cent.
A significant portion of these investments are concentrated in Malaysia Vision Valley 2.0 (MVV 2.0), which has emerged as one of the country's fastest-growing industrial corridors, supported by its proximity to Greater Kuala Lumpur, competitive land prices and improving infrastructure.
EcoWorld's Eco Business Park VII, located within MVV 2.0, has also recorded strong demand, achieving approximately RM2 billion in sales in less than a year since its launch in November 2025.
The company said enquiries for the industrial park remained elevated, with sustained interest from both domestic and foreign investors.
The MoU is valid for one year, with an option for renewal subject to mutual agreement between both parties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mr DIY shares under pressure on competition from Pinduoduo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MR DIY Group (M) Bhd's share price has come under renewed pressure amid concerns over intensifying competition from Chinese e-commerce platforms, especially Pinduoduo.
The counter ended five sen, or 4.55 per cent, lower at RM1.05, after opening at RM1.10 and touching an intraday low of RM1.05.
The latest decline brings MR DIY's year-to-date losses to 34.4 sen, or 23.8 per cent, while its forward price-to-earnings (PE) ratio has compressed to 15.8 times.
This compares with a valuation of more than 40 times when the company made its Bursa Malaysia debut on October 26, 2020, at an initial public offering (IPO) price of RM1.60 per share.
However, analyst sentiment remains largely positive, with several research houses maintaining 'Buy' recommendations on the retailer despite mounting competitive concerns.
CGS International Research believes concerns over the Chinese platform's competitive threat may be overstated.
The firm described Pinduoduo's free-shipping strategy as a temporary, subsidy-driven initiative rather than a structural threat to established retailers.
"We view Pinduoduo as a temporary headwind and do not expect free single item shipping to persist following E-Commerce Bill implementation, based on the precedent in Thailand.
"We believe the Malaysian government's potential introduction of the E-Commerce Bill in the next parliamentary session could benefit Mr DIY and other value retailers," it said.
CGS International maintained its 'Add' recommendation on MR DIY with a target price of RM1.90.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKFZ ready to open records, facilitate audits amid cooking oil traceability concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) says it is prepared to provide relevant reports and facilitate regulatory audits amid concerns over the origin, authenticity and traceability of cooking oil products allegedly blended before being re-exported under Malaysian labels.
PKFZ chairman Lim Lip Eng said the free zone would extend its full cooperation to the relevant authorities.
“We will provide our full cooperation and assistance, including making available relevant reports and facilitating any audit requests,” he said in a statement.
Lim said PKFZ operated under the Free Zones Act, while enforcement involving product authenticity and regulatory compliance fell under the jurisdiction of the relevant government agencies.
These include the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), SIRIM, the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) and the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB).
His response follows concerns raised last week by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan Ramasamy over the alleged blending of imported cooking oil with locally produced supplies before it is exported under Malaysian labels.
Jeyenderan said the alleged practice, which industry players have described as an oil “cocktail”, warranted closer scrutiny by the authorities, particularly over product origin, quality and food safety.
His remarks came after
The Edge
reported on Nov 4, citing industry sources, that imported palm oil was allegedly being blended with local supplies before being re-exported, potentially allowing foreign-origin oil to be marketed as Malaysian palm oil. According to the report, blending ratios of 75:25 or 80:20 were circulating in the market.
Jeyenderan said an examination of cargo manifests and bills of lading had raised concerns over how the oil’s country of origin was declared and how its actual composition was verified after blending.
Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, said independent laboratory tests were needed to establish whether the imported oil and the final blended product met the required quality and food safety standards.
He also questioned whether oil samples were tested before the vessels carrying the cargo left Malaysian waters, claiming the vessels concerned were not equipped with specialised laboratory facilities or qualified chemists to carry out detailed analyses.
Jeyenderan said any possibility of contamination should be investigated through scientific testing rather than assumptions.
“If the oil is contaminated, what could be the impact on public health? Who is responsible for ensuring that the final product is safe for consumption?” he had asked previously.
He said international rules already set clear expectations on origin, testing and traceability.
Under the Codex Alimentarius, the international food standards adopted by the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization and World Health Organization, the General Standard for the Labelling of Prepackaged Foods requires a food’s country of origin to be declared if leaving it out would mislead or deceive consumers.
“Codex only allows the origin to shift when processing changes the nature of the food. Simply mixing imported oil with Malaysian oil does not change its nature, so declaring the blend as wholly Malaysian may mislead buyers,” he was quoted saying.
On testing, he noted that international palm oil trade contracts under FOSFA International, including FOSFA Contract No. 81 issued jointly with the Palm Oil Refiners Association of Malaysia (PORAM), require independent analysis by qualified surveyors.
He also warned that Article 3 of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which will apply to large operators from December 30, 2026, requires palm oil entering the EU to be traceable to the plots of land where it was produced.
He urged the authorities to clarify the procedures governing the import, blending, sampling, quality certification and re-export of cooking oil, including which agencies are responsible for monitoring each stage.
He said proper documentation and independent laboratory testing were essential to ensure that products exported from Malaysia complied with the required standards and that their country of origin was accurately declared.
He added that failing to address the concerns could affect consumer confidence and Malaysia’s reputation as a food exporter.

Title: Najib’s house arrest: Malaysian Bar entitled to challenge Pardons Board decision, says Azalina
Article:
BANGI, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bar is entitled to mount such a challenge if it believes it has grounds to question the decision.
“But I have always stressed that when we speak of matters under Article 42, it is considered what is referred to as the prerogative of mercy, which we know is among the powers fully vested in the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the power of pardon.
“So it is up to the Malaysian Bar as to what it wants to bring... If the Malaysian Bar feels it has the right to question any issue, that is its right,” she told reporters here today.
She said this after the certificate presentation ceremony for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and Mediator Appointment Certificates, as well as the launch of the Madani Mediation Centre Handbook, Legal Aid Department 2026.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) today objected to the Malaysian Bar’s bid to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.
Senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly@Arwi informed High Court Judge S. Indra Nehru today that the AGC had received the Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review by email two days earlier and needed time to file written submissions.
Meanwhile, Najib’s lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee informed the court that his client also intended to file written submissions, as any decision by the court after leave is granted could affect him.
Lawyer Zainur Zakaria, representing the Malaysian Bar, did not object to the requests by the AGC and Najib’s lawyers for time to file their respective written submissions.
Judge Indra Nehru fixed March 17 next year to hear the application and directed both parties to file their respective written submissions by December 14, with replies to be filed on or before December 28.
On November 10, the Bar filed the judicial review application naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents. — Bernama

Title: Anwar joins Pakatan campaign trail in Melaka ahead of Saturday’s state polls
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined the coalition’s campaign trail in Melaka today as campaigning intensified ahead of Saturday’s state election.
The prime minister, who is also PKR president, began his campaign activities with a walkabout at shoplots and hawker stalls in Taman Krubong Jaya at about 6pm.
Accompanied by PH’s candidate for the Paya Rumput state seat, Datuk Azman Abidin, Anwar spent around 30 minutes mingling with hawkers, traders and residents, many of whom took the opportunity to greet him and take photographs.
He then proceeded to Kampung Machap Baru before attending the Ngopi Santai programme in Ayer Molek.
Anwar’s evening itinerary included the Melaka Rumah Kita programme at the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary service centre in Bukit Baru, followed by Melaka Rumah Kita carnival at Taman Melaka Perdana in Alor Gajah.
In the 16th Melaka polls, PH is fielding the most candidates, contesting 24 of the 28 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five) and Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (one). Three independent candidates are also contesting.
The Election Commission has set polling for Saturday, with 687,697 registered voters eligible to cast their ballots.
For the latest news on the state polls, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: KTMB: MyKomuter50 pass activation begins Nov 16, offering 30 days of unlimited travel on selected routes from Dec 1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The public can start activating the MyKomuter50 Pass on November 16 to enjoy unlimited travel for 30 days on selected KTM Komuter services for RM50, with savings of up to 88 per cent, effective December 1.
In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said the pass, aimed at easing the cost of living, was particularly beneficial to those commuting to work and educational institutions.
For example, users travelling on the Tanjung Malim-KL Sentral route, who would normally spend RM416 on fares over 30 days, would only need to pay RM50 with the pass, saving RM366 or nearly 88 per cent.
“For the Alor Setar-Butterworth route, users can save up to RM234, or about 82 per cent, compared with the estimated regular fare of RM284 over the same period and frequency of travel,” KTMB said.
The pass is open to Malaysian citizens aged seven and above who are not holders of the MyRailLife Pass. Applicants must present their MyKad or MyKid for eligibility verification.
Verification can be done through the KTM Mobile or KITS Style applications by uploading a copy of the identification document, a process that may take up to three working days.
Alternatively, users can obtain immediate verification at ticket kiosks or counters at KTM Komuter stations.
KTMB said activation and purchase facilities would be available at 34 selected stations, comprising 10 KTM Komuter Northern Sector stations, 20 Klang Valley KTM Komuter stations and four Southern Shuttle stations. An additional 11 registration counters would also be provided.
The pass is available at RM50 for each of the three service categories, namely MyKomuter50 Northern Sector, MyKomuter50 Klang Valley and MyKomuter50 Southern Shuttle.
KTMB encouraged users to complete the eligibility verification, activation and purchase processes on the same day.
Further information is available at www.ktmb.com.my or through the KTMB Call Centre at 03-9779 1200. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s FRIM puts century-old library collection online, opening 77,600 digital files to public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — More than a century’s worth of knowledge and information on tropical forest biodiversity and science from the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) is now accessible worldwide through its digital repository, the FRIM Research Depository (FRED).
FRIM said in a statement today that the FRED portal, fully operational since last year, recorded an average of 2,885 user accesses annually and offered free registration for round-the-clock access to 160,244 metadata records and 77,600 digital files.
The digital resources include scientific articles, books, theses, journals, forest maps and newspaper clippings, benefiting researchers, policymakers, industry players, students and the public.
“This digitalisation initiative marks a transformation from the physical services of the FRIM Library in Kepong, which receives an average of 2,200 visitors annually,” the statement said.
Established before 1918 and having survived both British and Japanese administrations, the specialised library houses nearly 200,000 reference materials covering 82 subjects related to forestry and forest products.
FRIM said historical records and documents preserved in the library were also among the key contributors to FRIM’s recognition as a Unesco World Heritage Site.
“To ensure authoritative and systematically organised scientific references, the library’s collection is managed using the Global Forestry Decimal Classification (GFDC), an international hierarchical classification standard also adopted by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the International Union of Forest Research Organisations (IUFRO),” the statement said.
Besides preserving heritage manuscripts from physical deterioration, the library houses four major special collections, namely the Rattan Collection, Bamboo Collection, Asean Collection and FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection.
According to FRIM, the Rattan Collection was developed in 1988 through the Rattan Information Centre (RIC), with funding from the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA), to promote rattan species such as Calamus manan as a scientific commodity and support rural economies.
The Bamboo Collection, established in 1993, contains more than 1,200 reference materials on bamboo research and industry, while the Asean Collection comprises research reports, proceedings on traditional forest management and studies on the regional impact of climate change.
Meanwhile, the FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection serves as the official repository of publications, consultancy reports and conference papers produced by FRIM researchers since 1990.
“Since the establishment of the Forestry School in 1927 and academic collaboration with the Faculty of Forestry at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) beginning in 1971, the FRIM Library has remained a cornerstone of human capital development and forestry education in the country.
“In today’s era of information overload, the FRED portal ensures that the public has access to authentic, reliable and rigorously evaluated scientific references,” the statement said.
Members of the public and the research community can explore the country’s wealth of tropical forest science knowledge through the FRED portal at
https://fred.frim.gov.my/Home/Index_v3
. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia selects Turkiye as preferred alternative missile supplier for Navy’s LCS project, says defence minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Turkiye has been selected as the preferred country to supply an alternative to Norway’s Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the decision was made after the government evaluated proposals from several countries, including Turkiye, France and Italy, based on price, delivery timelines and upfront costs.
“We have conducted an evaluation and have now reached the stage of determining that Turkiye is the best country from which to obtain an alternative to our missile.
“We will engage with the Turkish side for further negotiations so that we can finalise the matter,” he told reporters after the Defence Ministry’s 2026 Innovation Day celebration at the Mindef Auditorium today.
He said the government had also received assurances on the missile’s compatibility and integration with the ships’ systems, which would be further examined during negotiations with the Turkish company.
Mohamed Khaled said the missile from Turkiye was of the same type as that already ordered for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project, allowing supplies to be obtained earlier, as early as 2028.
He said the surface-to-surface missile had an operational range of 240 kilometres, with comparable explosive power and greater effectiveness than competing missiles.
In terms of cost, he said Malaysia would not have to bear the full cost of procuring new missiles, as part of the expense had already been absorbed under the LCS contract. Instead, the government would likely only need to cover the cost of installing the launchers and integrating the systems.
“If we did not have the LCS, we would have to order new missiles, which could cost RM700 million, RM800 million or RM900 million. Now, we do not need to spend that amount to replace the NSM,” he said.
On the procurement of the NSM from Norway, Mohamed Khaled said the project had stalled because the Norwegian government had not issued the required licence, meaning Malaysia would not receive the missiles despite having made payment for the procurement.
He said the government was now prepared to take legal action through arbitration, but was bound by several stages of dispute resolution stipulated in the contract, after initial negotiations reached a deadlock.
“We are therefore moving to the second stage, which is to establish a Dispute Resolution Committee between the two parties. If that process fails, Malaysia will proceed to arbitration, which can be held in Kuala Lumpur under the NSM procurement contract,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Khaled said Malaysia was not waiting for the process to be concluded before seeking a replacement for the NSM, to ensure that the country’s defence needs continued to be addressed while the process with Norway was ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysia must tap China ties to grow exports and open markets for local products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Malaysia should make the most of its strong ties with China to boost exports and expand markets for local products, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the Madani Government would continue to strengthen the business environment and help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) expand their reach in international markets.
“This will ensure that more local businesses benefit from the economic ties between the two countries,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Anwar received a courtesy call from the organising committee of the Malaysia-China Entrepreneurs Conference (MCEC) 2026, led by its adviser, Tan Sri Barry Goh Ming Choon, to discuss plans for the 16th edition of the prestigious conference.
Anwar said the government fully supported this year's conference as a strategic platform to strengthen trade, investment and business networks between the corporate communities of both countries.
“I hope MCEC will continue to open up more high-value economic opportunities, including helping local entrepreneurs and Bumiputera companies gain a foothold in the Chinese market, particularly in the halal industry,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Twelve Filipinos, including six children, detained in Labuan immigration crackdown
Article:
LABUAN, Nov 12 — Twelve Filipino nationals, including six children, were detained for suspected immigration offences during an enforcement operation on this duty-free island early today.
Labuan Immigration Department director Mohd Redzuan Nawi said the operation, codenamed Op Sapu, was conducted from 11pm yesterday to 1.30am today, involving 15 officers who inspected 84 individuals at several locations, including a residential settlement.
He said those inspected comprised 51 Malaysians, 31 Filipinos and two Indonesians.
“The 12 Filipinos detained comprised one man, five women, four boys and two girls, all suspected of offences under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63,” he told Bernama today.
Mohd Redzuan said two witness summonses were also issued to assist investigations.
